summary: Nuclear shape is measurable at scale from public 3D segmentations (Allen Cell hiPSC dataset, metadata.csv 1.69 GB; IDR MitoCheck 'nuclear shape' phenotype on 2,605 HeLa images) and qualitatively from HPA and CIL micrographs across cell types including muscle and secretory epithelia, but no public dataset pairs nuclear roundness with cytoplasmic stiffness, rheology or pressure anisotropy for the same cells. The HPA URL named by GPT (/humanproteome/cell) is now a 404; the section is /humanproteome/subcellular.
next_step: Compile a cell-type panel from HPA tissue images (skeletal muscle, goblet-cell epithelium, fibroblasts) scored for nuclear aspect ratio, and pair with published AFM/microrheology moduli per cell type from the literature; or seek a dataset combining Brillouin/AFM stiffness maps with nuclear segmentation.
obstacles_confirmed: Most image datasets lack matched cytoplasmic rheology or pressure.
Image archives rarely include a stiffness measurement for the same cell.
